lines.text: Measurements and units are essential for describing the physical world with precision. Length is measured in millimetres, centimetres, metres, and kilometres in the metric system, or inches, feet, yards, and miles in the imperial system. Weight uses grams, kilograms, and tonnes (metric) or ounces, pounds, and stones (imperial). Volume is measured in millilitres and litres (metric) or fluid ounces, pints, and gallons (imperial). The UK uses a confusing mix of both systems: road distances are in miles, height is often in feet and inches, weight can be in stones and pounds, but food is sold in grams and kilograms. Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius (°C) or Fahrenheit (°F). Speed combines distance and time: kilometres per hour (km/h) or miles per hour (mph). Area is measured in square metres (m²) or square feet (ft²), and land in hectares or acres. Time units range from seconds and minutes to hours, days, weeks, and years. Understanding how to express measurements in English — including the prepositions and vocabulary around them — is vital for cooking, travel, shopping, science, construction, and countless everyday situations.

lines.text: The UK uniquely mixes metric and imperial: roads use miles, beer comes in pints, people give their weight in stones, but shops sell food in kilograms and litres. This dual system confuses both natives and learners!
lines.name: The UK uniquely mixes metric and imperial: roads use miles, beer comes in pints, people give their weight in stones, but shops sell food in kilograms and litres. This dual system confuses both natives and learners!

lines.text: In the UK (but not the US), body weight is often given in 'stones' (1 stone = 14 pounds ≈ 6.35 kg). '10 stone 5' means 10 stones and 5 pounds (about 66 kg). Americans use pounds only.

lines.text: Though both use 'imperial' units, UK and US gallons differ: a UK gallon = 4.546 litres, a US gallon = 3.785 litres. UK pints are also larger. This causes genuine confusion when following recipes or comparing fuel economy.
